messages:
sara (Support): Hey team — customer acme-inc is reporting intermittent 502/504s hitting our hosted /v1/generate streaming endpoint since ~2024-11-03T18:12Z. Happening mostly on long-lived streams (30s+). Sample req id: req_01H3XJ6Z. They provided a curl repro.

mohit (Eng-SRE): Can you paste the exact curl and a trace id? also is this only for that tenant or global? :eyes:

sara (Support): curl: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"stream test","stream":true}' \n  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate`
Trace id from customer: trace-acme-20241103-1812. They say ~10% of streams get a 502 or hang then 504.

ops-bot: alert:edge-gateway: upstream-reset-rate spike detected for cluster=hostedapi-edge ; window=5m ; rate=28/s (threshold=10/s) — https://app.metrics/edges/alerts/1123

mohit (Eng-SRE): Thanks. I'm seeing corresponding envoy upstream_reset and HTTP2 RST_STREAM logs around those times. Likely h2 stream resets from the auth upstream under burst. Running quick metric query: `sum(rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_total{response_code!~"2.."}[5m])) by (cluster)` -> cluster=auth-cache shows spike.

jade (Eng-Runtime): Could be interplay between long streaming sessions + auth cache eviction + windowing on the frontdoor. If auth responses intermittently 5xx or take >1s we see h2 connection eviction. Can you share an example span?

sara (Support): Paste from customer logs: `upstream error: stream reset EPROTO, upstream_status=502, bytes_sent=0, req_id=req_01H3XJ6Z`

mohit (Eng-SRE): Repro attempt from my client (non-prod) using a large stream payload: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -N ... & sleep 0.05; done` — I'm seeing ~12 failures in 200 (6%). Attaching envoy logs snippet: `envoy error: h2 stream aborted: rst_code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, upstream_reset=true`

jade (Eng-Runtime): ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM on our stack usually means upstream closed connection due to backpressure. Two mitigation angles: 1) reduce per-tenant concurrency window on ingest, 2) add short-lived fallback to smaller model variant for heavy streams. Also check auth-cache TTL and k/v eviction churn.

mohit (Eng-SRE): I've increased the auth upstream connection pool to 200 for the affected cluster and bumped keepalive timeout to 90s for one node group (temporary). Patch applied: `kubectl patch cm envoy-edge-config -p '{"data":{"max_concurrent_streams":"200"}}'` — will monitor. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy:edge-config v2.14.8 rolled at 2024-11-03T18:10Z by @infra-deploy; release notes mention h2 tuning changes.

lina (Product): Customer SLA flagged. They want a mitigation ASAP or to be moved to a dedicated pool. What is ETA on stabilization?

mohit (Eng-SRE): After the pool bump error rate dropped to ~3% in my repro. I'll keep the change live for 30m and watch. If we see re-escalation we should route that tenant to dedicated capacity as a failover.

jade (Eng-Runtime): Also rolling a small runtime change to gate long-running KV cache validations to avoid eviction storms on auth reads. I'll open a PR and can hotfix if needed.

sara (Support): I told acme-inc we applied a tuning change and asked for confirmation. Waiting on their reproducer run.

ops-bot: metrics:update edge-gateway/upstream_reset_rate cluster=auth-cache -> drop from 28/s to 4/s over 10m

mohit (Eng-SRE): Customer confirmed fewer failures in latest run (from ~10% -> ~1.5%). I'll keep monitoring for 1h then close. If it resurfaces we'll schedule tenant migration and deeper root cause debug (auth cache eviction policy + envoy h2 windowing).

sara (Support): Thanks — I'll send a summary to the customer and cc @lina. Closing here once monitor window passes. :white_check_mark:
